author: pgaudet
body:
### From Claude 

**Gene:** C. elegans ndx-4, WB:WBGene00003581 / UniProtKB:Q9U2M7 (Nudix hydrolase; asymmetrical Ap4A hydrolase; PANTHER PTHR21340:SF0)

A literature review of ndx-4 suggests removing several existing BP annotations as over-interpretations and adding the MutT-type (8-oxo-(d)GTPase) activity, which is not annotated yet.

Full text was read for PMID:24435662 only. PMIDs 11738085, 12475970, 12370170, 11937063, 21111690 and 24347047 were assessed from abstracts.

## Existing annotations to remove

| GO term | Evidence / ref | Source | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| GO:0006167 AMP biosynthetic process | IDA PMID:11738085, IDA PMID:12475970, IBA | WB, GO_Central | AMP/ATP are products of Ap4A **catabolism**. There is no evidence that NDX-4 contributes to cellular adenine-nucleotide synthesis. GO:0015967 diadenosine tetraphosphate catabolic process already captures the process. |
| GO:0006754 ATP biosynthetic process | IDA PMID:11738085, IDA PMID:12475970, IBA | WB, GO_Central | Same as above. |
| GO:0006172 ADP biosynthetic process | IDA PMID:11738085 | WB | Same as above (ADP would come from Ap5A/Ap6A hydrolysis). |
| GO:0019693 ribose phosphate metabolic process | IDA PMID:12370170 | WB | Based only on an in vitro PRPP hydrolysis assay. The authors propose PRPP as a significant substrate only for D. radiodurans DR2356 and the DIPP subfamily, not for Ap4A hydrolases. The MF GO:0043135 is sufficient. |
| GO:0006915 apoptotic process | TAS PMID:11937063 | UniProt | Crystal-structure paper. The abstract only says the enzyme "potentially" influences apoptosis via the Ap3A/Ap4A ratio; there is no experiment. Note: human NUDT2 (P50583) has an ISS to GO:0006915 citing the same paper, which should also be reviewed. |

**PAINT:** the IBAs to AMP/ATP biosynthetic process on PTHR21340 seem to propagate from the worm IDAs above. Please review.

## Existing annotations confirmed
- GO:0004081 bis(5'-nucleosyl)-tetraphosphatase (asymmetrical) activity: IDA PMID:11738085, IDA PMID:12475970, IBA
- GO:0015967 diadenosine tetraphosphate catabolic process: IDA PMID:11738085, PMID:12475970
- GO:0043135 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate pyrophosphatase activity: IDA PMID:12370170. Kept: a real but likely minor in vitro activity; the C. elegans active-site mutants lack it.

## Suggested new annotations

**MF**
- **GO:0035539** 8-oxo-7,8-dihydrodeoxyguanosine triphosphate diphosphatase activity, IDA
  - PMID:24435662, Table I: purified NDX-4 hydrolysed 59.5% of 20 µM 8-oxo-dGTP in 30 min (HPLC), and did not hydrolyse 8-oxo-dGDP.
  - PMID:21111690: "ability to hydrolyze 8-oxodGTP".
  - The products (8-oxo-dGMP + PPi) should be confirmed in the PMID:21111690 full text before using this exact term.
- **GO:0008413** 8-oxo-7,8-dihydroguanosine triphosphate pyrophosphatase activity (8-oxo-GTP → 8-oxo-GDP + Pi), IDA PMID:24435662
  - Table I shows 34.3% hydrolysis.
  - Methods: "8-oxo-GDP was prepared as the product of hydrolysis of 8-oxo-GTP by NDX-4".

**BP**
- **GO:0042262** DNA protection, from PMID:21111690:
  - NDX-4 suppresses the E. coli mutT mutator phenotype (heterologous complementation).
  - Loss of ndx-4 compromises genomic stability in vivo (IMP).
  - Human NUDT1/MTH1 carries the same term.
  - Supporting data in PMID:24435662: ndx-4(ok1003) worms are hypersensitive to menadione bisulfite and methyl viologen, and chk-2/clk-2 RNAi rescues the larval sensitivity.
- *For discussion:* GO:0006979 response to oxidative stress, IMP PMID:24435662. This is a hypersensitivity phenotype of a pool-sanitizing enzyme. DNA protection may be the better fit.

## Note on propagation
The 8-oxo-(d)GTPase activity of NDX-4 is probably Nudix substrate ambiguity, not shared by descent with MutT/NUDT1. Human NUDT2 has no experimental evidence for it, so it should not be propagated across PTHR21340 without data.

author: pgaudet
body: Fixed PAINT IBAs: removed GO:0006167 AMP biosynthetic process and GO:0006754 ATP biosynthetic process, and added GO:0015967 diadenosine tetraphosphate catabolic process.

author: vanaukenk
body: @pgaudet - I'm starting to work on this; thanks for the report.

author: vanaukenk
body:
@pgaudet  - I've removed all of the existing BPs in the table above from ndx-4.

I'm reviewing the MFs from all of the papers again, though, as it's possible we'll need a new MF term.

author: cmungall
body:
ai-gene-review for ndx-4

https://ai4curation.io/ai-gene-review/genes/worm/ndx-4/ndx-4-ai-review.html

it consistently flags the same annotations, but it is much more qualified in the new MF; we really need better guidelines for substrate specficity here.

author: vanaukenk
body:
@cmungall - I've already added the suggested new MF annotation and had already put on the agenda for my call with @pgaudet tomorrow to talk about guidelines for substrate specificity wrt annotation.

It was also be more helpful if the gene review tool talked to the live curation database (in this case Protein2GO) so it knows ASAP what changes curators have made.
